00 — Financial Data Lakehouse, Document Intelligence & Governed AI: Index

The one idea: a trustworthy financial data platform keeps every source file untouched, turns it into open Iceberg tables that remember both when a fact was true and when it was known, has people certify what is published, and lets AI agents answer only from certified data through deterministic tools. This set teaches each piece in the order you need it, and ends with a ten-phase build you can run on a laptop.

1. What this set covers

The stack, from the bottom up:

Layer Technologies
Domain ISIN, CIN, PAN, LEI, AMFI codes; SEBI, RBI, BRSR, ECL, NPA
Single-machine data stack Pydantic, Polars, DuckDB, Apache Arrow
Storage Object storage (S3 / MinIO), SHA-256 content addressing, WORM Object Lock
Lakehouse Apache Parquet, Apache Iceberg, PyIceberg, REST catalogs (Lakekeeper, Polaris, Unity Catalog)
Data management ODCS data contracts, quality gates, bitemporal modelling, entity resolution (Splink, RapidFuzz), FIBO ontology, NetworkX graphs
Documents Docling, MinerU, PaddleOCR, vision-language models, GLiNER, FinBERT
AI MCP, hybrid RAG (Qdrant / pgvector, BM25, rerankers), LiteLLM gateway, MLflow tracing, RAGAS
Runtime Java 21, Spring Boot 3 modular monolith, ServiceLoader plug-ins, OpenFeign, Redis, Flowable BPMN, SSE

It assumes you can write Python and SQL. Related sets elsewhere in the knowledge base:

  • Data Engineering — Spark, Delta Lake, streaming and orchestration.
  • Open Lakehouse — goes further on Iceberg v3 deletes, Parquet and Arrow, Unity Catalog and Databricks services. Read this set first for the step-by-step basics, then that one for depth.
  • AI Engineering — building MCP servers, agents and evaluations in general.
  • Polars deep dive and LLM engineering and RAG.

2. Chapter map

# Chapter What you get from it
01 Financial Domain Foundations Identifiers with validators, regulators, credit-risk and mutual-fund vocabulary, the three dates on every fact
02 Pydantic, Polars and DuckDB Typed validation, lazy dataframes, as-of joins, serverless SQL over files
03 Object Storage and Immutable Landing Content-addressed landing, manifests, rights register, S3 Object Lock on MinIO, the collector
04 The Data Lakehouse Definition, history, layers, what is on disk, table formats compared, medallion, a minimal local build
05 Apache Iceberg Internals Metadata tree, read and commit paths, snapshots, tags, branches, hidden partitioning, schema evolution, COW/MOR, maintenance
06 Working with Iceberg: PyIceberg, Polars and DuckDB Create, append, overwrite, upsert, delete, transactions, time travel, tags, evolution — all tested code
07 Iceberg REST Catalogs The REST protocol, Lakekeeper/Polaris/Unity Catalog, local setup, connecting Spark/Trino/DuckDB, credential vending
08 Data Contracts and Quality Gates ODCS v3, datacontract-cli, rule categories, rules as data, quarantine, atomic publish
09 Bitemporal Modelling Valid vs knowledge time, update/correction/restatement, append-only design, as-of queries
10 Entity Resolution, Ontology and Graphs Three-tier matching, Fellegi–Sunter with Splink, survivorship, FIBO, contagion graphs
11 Document Intelligence and Financial NLP Layout and table parsing, OCR and VLMs, bounding boxes, GLiNER, FinBERT, evidence records
12 Governed AI Agents: MCP, Hybrid RAG and the AI Gateway Deterministic tools over MCP, hybrid retrieval with provenance, gateway controls, tracing and evaluation
13 Java Modular Monolith and Workflows SPI plug-ins, Feign/Eureka/Redis, maker-checker with Flowable, eight-step turn over SSE
14 Hands-On Build Plan Ten phases, each with what to build and how to know it works

4. Conventions used in this set

  • All code is runnable on a laptop with free, open-source tools; sample identifiers and companies are fictional.
  • Time intervals are half-open [from, to), with 9999-12-31 as the open end.
  • "Certified" means approved by a second person and pinned as an Iceberg tag.
  • Each chapter ends with Questions to test yourself and a Review checklist.
